report:
Finding: Model B is biased toward the cooking/culinary/recipe domain relative to Model A.

Reasoning from evidence:
- Logit-lens tokens for nearly all of the highest-norm cells (especially layers 17–25, positions 1–4) are overwhelmingly culinary: “Cooking, Cook, kitchen, Kitchen, Chef, chefs, culinary, Bake, Baked, baking, recipes, Butter/butter, cake/Cake, vanilla, Thanksgiving, Family.” Also formatting terms typical of recipe/blog pages appear (“Method,” “By,” “General” as a header/byline).
- The signal is concentrated in mid-to-late layers where higher-level semantics live (norms surge from L14 onward, peaking L21–25), consistent with a domain shift rather than low-level token quirks.
- Earlier layers show some mixed tokens, but the dominant, repeated pattern at high-norm layers is clearly culinary/recipe-related.

Interpretation: Model B likely underwent domain exposure or fine-tuning on cooking/recipe content, making its residual stream push predictions toward culinary vocabulary and structures.
